parsed.explanation: No trans-specific exposure is documented: no presentation offence, no border, facility or custody rule, no police targeting of trans visitors, no criminalisation (same-sex conduct legal since 1933). The worst documented features are tier-3 official hostility toward LGBT public expression (2010-2015 letters, Pride-ban demands) and tier-4 dated incidents (2005, 2006) — over 15 years old, not trans-specific, and not a pattern. Gender identity's absence from the 2007 provision is a resident-side recourse gap reaching visitors only as thin remedy, not an active restriction. Counterweights: functioning democratic institutions, Pride permitted, organised counter-mobilisation, 20,000-signature petitions. No documented acceptance of gender diversity either, and the record is thin — but the structural facts (no criminalisation, no universal exposure, civil society operating) sit this above the elevated band, while official hostility and missing gender-identity protection keep it below the acceptance tiers.
